43:We'll start by morphing a thumbnail into a hero image (shared elements), then animate the loading skeleton into real content (Suspense reveals), add directional slides for forward and back navigation (route transitions), and finish with crossfades for switching between photographer tabs (same-route transitions).
50:View transitions work in the App Router with no configuration. The App Router uses [React canary releases](https://react.dev/blog/2023/05/03/react-canaries), which contain all stable React 19 changes as well as newer features like `ViewTransition`. You do not need to install `react@canary` yourself.

61:`<ViewTransition>` animations are activated by [Transitions](https://react.dev/reference/react/useTransition), [`<Suspense>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense), and [`useDeferredValue`](https://react.dev/reference/react/useDeferredValue). Regular `setState` calls do not trigger them. In Next.js, route navigations are transitions, so `<ViewTransition>` animations activate automatically during navigation.

103:    </ViewTransition>

121:</ViewTransition>
124:Add the same props to both Step 1 snippets (`photo-grid.tsx` and `photo-content.tsx`). `default="none"` keeps each named image from running its own crossfade on every unrelated transition. Without it, every named `<ViewTransition>` animates whenever any transition runs on the page. When you add `default="none"` to a named pair, keep the explicit `share`. With `default="none"` and no `share` prop, the pair silently stops morphing.
142:### Step 2: Animate loading states with Suspense reveals
144:The photo detail page loads its content asynchronously. While data is in flight, a Suspense boundary shows a skeleton. When the data resolves, the skeleton is replaced by the real content.
146:Without a transition, the swap is instant. The skeleton vanishes and the content pops in.
150:Wrap the Suspense fallback in a `ViewTransition` with an exit animation, and the content in a `ViewTransition` with an enter animation:

263:</ViewTransition>

When a navigation carries the `nav-forward` type, the exit animation slides old content left and the enter animation slides new content in from the right. The `default: "none"` ensures that transitions without a type (browser back/forward, `router.refresh()`, Suspense reveals) produce no directional animation.

285:</ViewTransition>

events.content:
Implemented — the gallery now uses React/Next view transitions end-to-end.

**What Changed**
- Shared-image morph: wrapped grid thumbnail and detail hero in matching `ViewTransition` names (`product-image-${slug}`) with `share="morph"` so the image smoothly morphs between routes.
- Directional page slides: added page-level `ViewTransition` wrappers with `enter/exit` maps for `nav-forward` and `nav-back`, plus `transitionTypes` on links (`forward` on product cards, `back` on return link).
- Smooth suspense handoff: wrapped suspense fallback/content with `exit="slide-down"` and `enter="slide-up"` transitions so skeletons yield smoothly to real content.
- Reduced motion support: added `prefers-reduced-motion` rules that disable transition durations/delays and stop skeleton pulsing animations.

**Updated Files**
- `app/ProductGrid.tsx:1`
- `app/page.tsx:1`
- `app/product/[slug]/page.tsx:1`
- `app/globals.css:7`

**Validation**
- `npm run build` passes successfully.

If you want, I can also tune the motion timings/easing to match a specific brand feel (snappier, softer, etc.).

**Summarizing implementation and validation**

**What I changed**  
- Implemented shared element morph between grid and detail with matching names.  
- Added directional slide transitions for page navigation using ViewTransition wrappers and Link transitionTypes.  
- Enabled smooth suspense fallback transitions with slide and fade animations on home and detail boundaries.  
- Incorporated CSS for timing, morph blur, pointer event passthrough, and respected reduced-motion media query disabling animations.  
- Updated main classes affecting page-shell and main style, reverted tsconfig changes, and left package-lock.json removed as it was previously untracked.

**Files**  
- `app/ProductGrid.tsx:1`  
- `app/product/[slug]/page.tsx:1`  
- `app/page.tsx:1`  
- `app/globals.css:7`

**Validation**  
- Build runs and passes (`npm run build`), generating `.next` and related files; these were cleaned afterward to avoid diff noise.  
- React runtime includes ViewTransition support as needed.
